en: Why should I wash my hands?
Does handwashing prevent disease?
Why does washing hands matter?

answer_short.en: Handwashing removes germs that spread diarrhoea, cholera, and other diseases.
answer_short.shona: Kugeza maoko kunobvisa masimu anoparadzira manyoka, korora, nezvimwe zvirwere.

answer_warning.en: Not washing hands can spread disease to you and other people.
answer_warning.shona: Kusageza maoko kunogona kuparadzira chirwere kwamuri nekune vamwe.

canonical_question.en: When should I wash my hands?

en: What times should I wash my hands?
When is handwashing needed?
When must I wash hands?

answer_short.en: Wash your hands at important times to stop germs from spreading.
answer_short.shona: Gezai maoko panguva dzinokosha kuti masimu arege kupararira.

en: Wash before eating or preparing food.
Wash after using the toilet or changing a baby's nappy.
Wash before feeding a child and after touching animals or waste.
shona: Gezai maoko musati madya kana kugadzira chikafu.
Gezai mushure mekushandisa chimbuzi kana kuchinja nappy yemwana.
Gezai musati madyisa mwana uye mushure mekubata mhuka kana tsvina.

canonical_question.en: How do I wash my hands properly?

en: What is the right way to wash hands?
Show me how to wash hands.
How should I clean my hands?

answer_short.en: Wash all parts of your hands well with clean water and soap or ash.
answer_short.shona: Gezai zvikamu zvose zvemaoko nemvura yakachena nesipo kana madota.

en: Wet your hands with clean water.
Rub with soap or ash for at least 20 seconds, including between fingers.
Rinse well and dry with a clean cloth or in the air.
shona: Kwizai nesipo kana madota kwemasekondi anopfuura makumi maviri, kusanganisira pakati peminwe.
Sukutai zvakanaka moomesa nejira rakachena kana nemhepo.

answer_warning.en: Rinsing with water alone is not enough to remove germs well.
answer_warning.shona: Kungosukuta nemvura chete hazvibvisi masimu zvakanaka.

canonical_question.en: What should I do if I do not have soap?

en: How do I wash hands without soap?
I have no soap.
What can I use instead of soap?
shona: Ndinogeza sei maoko kana pasina sipo?

answer_short.en: You can use clean ash when soap is not available.
answer_short.shona: Munogona kushandisa madota akachena kana sipo isipo.

en: Wet your hands with clean water.
Rub your hands with ash for at least 20 seconds.
Rinse well with clean water and dry them.
shona: Kwizai maoko nemadota kwemasekondi anopfuura makumi maviri.

answer_warning.en: Do not skip handwashing because soap is not available.
answer_warning.shona: Musarega kugeza maoko nokuti sipo haisipo.

canonical_question.en: I do not have soap, what should I do?

en: No soap is available.
What do I do without soap?
I cannot find soap for washing hands.

answer_short.en: If soap is not available, use ash and still wash your hands properly.
answer_short.shona: Kana sipo isipo, shandisai madota uye muchiri kugeza maoko zvakanaka.

en: Wet your hands with clean water.
Rub ash over all parts of your hands for 20 seconds.
Rinse well and dry with a clean cloth or air.
shona: Kwizai madota pazvikamu zvose zvemaoko kwemasekondi makumi maviri.
Sukutai zvakanaka moomesa nejira rakachena kana nemhepo.

answer_warning.en: Ash is better than not washing your hands at all.
answer_warning.shona: Madota ari nani pane kurega kugeza maoko zvachose.
